clinical.citation: Biallelic PDE2A variants: a new cause of syndromic paroxysmal dyskinesia. (PMID: 32467598)

variants.description: c.1922+5G>A splice-site compound heterozygous (out of frame transcript lacking exon 22)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Trio whole-exome sequencing; biallelic variants segregating with disease; mitochondria network morphology changes in patient fibroblasts; loss-of-function confirmed by transcript analysis

clinical.citation: A homozygous loss-of-function mutation in PDE2A associated to early-onset hereditary chorea. (PMID: 29392776)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Trio whole-exome sequencing; homozygous variant in GAF-B domain; severely decreased enzymatic activity of PDE2A confirmed functionally; negative for NKX2-1, ADCY5, PDE10A mutations

clinical.citation: A homozygous founder variant in PDE2A causes paroxysmal dyskinesia with intellectual disability. (PMID: 37317634)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Whole exome sequencing; variant segregates with disease in three consanguineous Pakistani families; haplotype analysis revealed 3.16 Mb shared founder haplotype at 11q13.4; novel missense variant absent from controls

clinical.citation: ASHG 2022 - Biallelic founder mutation in PDE2A causes paroxysmal dyskinesia with Intellectual disability in Pakistani families (A. Fatima, H. Yousaf, S. Baig, I. zafar, M. Toft)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Whole exome sequencing; variant segregates with phenotype in all three families; homozygosity mapping revealed shared 5.5 Mb homozygous region at Chr11:q13.4-q13.5 consistent with founder effect; rare variant

clinical.citation: Motor, epileptic, and developmental phenotypes in genetic disorders affecting G protein coupled receptors-cAMP signaling. (PMID: 36003298)

biological.citation: Gene therapy with phosphodiesterases 2A and 4B ameliorates heart failure and arrhythmias by improving subcellular cAMP compartmentation (PMID: 38776406)
biological.summary: AAV9-mediated overexpression of PDE2A3 in a mouse pressure-overload heart failure model attenuated cardiac hypertrophy, fibrosis, and contractile decline. Live cell imaging with targeted cAMP biosensors showed PDE2A overexpression restored altered cAMP compartmentation in caveolin-rich plasma membrane microdomains, accompanied by ameliorated caveolin-3 decline and antiarrhythmic effects under isoproterenol stimulation.

biological.citation: Activation of PDE2A moderates pathologically high cAMP/PKA responses to dopamine in dyskinetic mice (PMID: 40412662)
biological.summary: In the 6-OHDA mouse model of Parkinson's disease, cAMP and PKA signaling were markedly upregulated in striatal neurons. Stimulation of cGMP signaling by a NO donor (DEANO) efficiently down-regulated these hypersensitive cAMP/PKA responses via PDE2A activation, demonstrating that cGMP-stimulated PDE2A activity can moderate excessive D1 receptor-driven cAMP/PKA signaling in the striatum.

biological.citation: miR-139/PDE2A-Notch1 feedback circuit represses stemness of gliomas by inhibiting Wnt/β-catenin signaling (PMID: 34512162)
biological.summary: PDE2A overexpression in patient-derived glioma stem-like cells suppressed stemness by inhibiting cAMP accumulation and GSK-3β phosphorylation, thereby reducing Wnt/β-catenin signaling and self-renewal. Both PDE2A and its co-transcribed miR-139 were inversely correlated with glioma stem cell stemness and associated with better prognosis in clinical samples. Targeted delivery of PDE2A via OCP liposomes significantly repressed stemness and decelerated glioma progression in orthotopic xenograft models.

biological.citation: Defects in AMPAR trafficking and microglia activation underlie socio-cognitive deficits associated to decreased expression of phosphodiesterase 2A (PMID: 38154608)
biological.summary: Pde2a+/- mice (homozygous knockouts are non-viable) displayed sex-dependent socio-cognitive deficits, with males showing severe deficits throughout life and females showing milder adult-onset cognitive impairment. In males, these phenotypes were associated with microglia activation, elevated glutathione levels, and increased GluR1 externalization in CA1, producing reduced mGluR-dependent long-term depression, revealing PDE2A-dependent molecular targets underlying socio-cognitive performance.

biological.citation: PDE2A Inhibition Enhances Axonal Sprouting, Functional Connectivity, and Recovery after Stroke (PMID: 36163142)
biological.summary: Pharmacological inhibition of PDE2A in a mouse cortical stroke model enhanced functional recovery of the contralateral forelimb, increased axonal projections in peri-infarct cortex, and improved functional connectivity of motor system excitatory neurons as measured by two-photon in vivo imaging. PDE2A inhibition did not affect angiogenesis, gliogenesis, neurogenesis, or inflammatory responses, suggesting its pro-recovery effects are specifically mediated through neuronal connectivity mechanisms.

biological.citation: Phosphodiesterases PDE2A and PDE10A both change mRNA expression in the human brain with age, but only PDE2A changes in a region-specific manner with psychiatric disease (PMID: 32119913)
biological.summary: Using autoradiographic in situ hybridization on postmortem brain tissue, PDE2A mRNA was found to be reduced in the amygdala of patients with schizophrenia, MDD, and bipolar disorder, while frontal cortical reductions were specific to schizophrenia and hippocampal/striatal reductions were most pronounced in bipolar disorder. PDE2A mRNA expression increased across brain development, and its region- and disorder-specific changes implicate it as a potential diagnostic biomarker or therapeutic target in psychiatric disease.
biological.sample_size: Stanley Foundation Neuropathology Consortium postmortem cohort

biological.citation: PDE2A Is Indispensable for Mouse Liver Development and Hematopoiesis (PMID: 32326334)
biological.summary: PDE2A knockout mice are embryonic lethal, and at E14.5 their livers are extremely reduced in size with loss of niche integrity, compromised hematopoietic function, and apoptosis in hepatoblasts and endothelial/stromal compartments. Increased intracellular cAMP and upregulation of the inducible cAMP early repressor (ICER) in PDE2A-/- livers likely impairs development by downregulating the anti-apoptotic gene Bcl2, establishing PDE2A as essential for liver niche integrity and hematopoiesis.

biological.citation: Critical role of phosphodiesterase 2A in mouse congenital heart defects (PMID: 29409032)
biological.summary: PDE2A knockout embryos exhibited cardiac defects including absence of atrial trabeculation, interventricular septum defects, hypertrabeculation, myocardial wall thinning, and occasionally overriding aorta and valve defects. Loss of PDE2A caused increased intracellular cAMP, upregulation of ICER, downregulation of Tbx transcription factors, reduced cardiomyocyte proliferation, and increased apoptosis, demonstrating a direct role for PDE2A-mediated cAMP regulation in cardiac development.

biological.citation: Involvement of Phosphodiesterase 2A Activity in the Pathophysiology of Fragile X Syndrome (PMID: 30137253)
biological.summary: PDE2A enzymatic activity is increased in the brain of Fmr1-KO mice (a Fragile X Syndrome model), leading to decreased cAMP and cGMP levels, as PDE2A mRNA is a prominent target of FMRP. Pharmacological inhibition of PDE2A in Fmr1-KO mice rescued dendritic spine maturity, hippocampal mGluR-dependent LTD, and social/communicative deficits in both mouse and rat models, with chronic neonatal inhibition followed by washout rescuing adolescent social behavior.

biological.citation: Differential expression of the cyclic GMP-stimulated phosphodiesterase PDE2A in human venous and capillary endothelial cells (PMID: 10375378)
biological.summary: Using selective monoclonal antibodies, PDE2A protein was detected in cerebellum, neocortex, heart, kidney, lung, pulmonary artery, and skeletal muscle. Immunocytochemical analysis revealed PDE2A expression specifically in venous and capillary endothelial cells but not in arterial endothelial cells of cardiac and renal tissue, with expression also present in microvascular endothelial cells of renal glomerulus, skin, brain, and liver, suggesting a role in modulating cyclic nucleotide effects on endothelial barrier function.
